chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Isma'il ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both)

That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand words, each word opening up to one thousand [new] words, so the people do not know what he had taught him.

key_terms.فَمَا يُدْرِي النَّاسُ: so the people do not know

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the thousand words taught to Imam Ali by the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the concept of *al-Kalimat al-Mufassalah* (detailed words), illustrating the infinite depth of Imam Ali’s knowledge as the inheritor of the Prophet’s esoteric wisdom. It underscores the Shia belief that the Ahl al-Bayt possess a comprehensive understanding of the Quran and divine law that transcends the general comprehension of the broader community. The metaphor of 'a thousand words unlocking a thousand more' emphasizes the generative and boundless nature of this sacred knowledge.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-37 Al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, Ali ibn Isma’il ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qad’dah, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), “
God’s Prophet (MGB) taught Ali (MGB) one-thousand words each of which opened up to one-thousand new words. He did not tell the people what the Prophet (MGB) had taught him.”
